title: Virgin and Child
license: Public Domain（馆方标注为公共领域）
sourceNote: 中文简介据大都会艺术博物馆作品页整理（2026-10-04）；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
artistZh: 巴托洛梅·埃斯特班·穆里略
museumZh: 纽约大都会艺术博物馆
descriptionZh: 穆里略用柔和的明暗和自然的动作，让传统的圣母子题材显得亲近。婴儿似乎在吃奶时忽然转头，仿佛注意到了画外的观众。馆方介绍指出，这幅画的摹本曾为墨西哥画家比利亚尔潘多所知；他把相同的人物形象用进了当地教堂的作品。
lookForZh: 先看婴儿转向画外的目光，再看母亲低头注视他的姿态。比较人物柔和的轮廓与暗背景，体会画家怎样营造亲密的气氛。

title: View of Toledo
license: Public Domain（馆方标注为公共领域）
sourceNote: 中文简介据大都会艺术博物馆作品页整理（2026-10-04）；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
museumZh: 纽约大都会艺术博物馆
descriptionZh: 托莱多是画家长期生活和工作的城市。这幅约1599—1600年的风景画采用了重新安排的城市布局：大教堂被移到更醒目的位置，建筑与山丘也经过变形。阴沉的天空、明亮的绿色和强烈明暗，让熟悉的城市呈现出紧张而富有情绪的气氛。
lookForZh: 先看天空的暗色与山坡的亮绿，再找突出天际线的建筑。观察扭曲的形状怎样让静止的风景显得不平静。

title: Portrait of Dora Wheeler
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 朵拉·惠勒是蔡斯从慕尼黑回到纽约后招收的第一位学生，当时愿意私下教授女性的美国画家还不多。后来，她与母亲创办了一家完全由女性经营的装饰设计公司，自己负责华美的织物设计。肖像背景中的刺绣丝织挂毯呼应了她的职业。这幅画在1883年的慕尼黑展览上获金奖，后来由惠勒本人捐给博物馆。
lookForZh: 先看人物与身后大面积织物的关系，再观察挂毯的花纹和衣服的质感。背景既是装饰，也提示了她从事的设计工作。

title: Stag at Sharkey's
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 贝洛斯描绘的是纽约沙基体育俱乐部的拳击赛，这家设有后室拳台的酒馆就在他的画室附近。当时纽约禁止公开拳击比赛，赛事往往以私人俱乐部活动的形式举行。外来选手需要临时入会，标题中的“stag”就指这种参赛者。馆方把作品放在拳击由工人阶层娱乐逐渐吸引更广泛观众的时代背景中理解。
lookForZh: 先沿拳手身体交错的方向观察力量如何碰撞，再看周围观众的反应。试着比较拳台内的身体动作与台外密集的人群，体会这场比赛的紧张感。

title: The Biglin Brothers Turning the Stake
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 这幅画记录了1872年5月费城斯库尔基尔河上的一次著名赛艇比赛。巴尼和约翰·比格林兄弟正在绕过标志赛程中点的木桩，右侧中景中的对手已落在后面。他们最终赢得比赛。伊金斯用细致准备的人体和透视研究组织画面，把两人协作与真实的运动场景结合起来。
lookForZh: 先找出木桩、兄弟的赛艇和右侧对手的位置，理解转弯的路线，再观察两名划手的身体与船桨如何配合。远处岸边的观众让这次竞赛有了具体的现场感。

title: The Race Track (Death on a Pale Horse)
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
titleZh: 赛马场（骑苍白马的死神）
descriptionZh: 馆方记载，这幅画受到1888年纽约一场赛马及其悲剧后果的触动：画家的一位朋友下注失利后自尽。莱德用带有中世纪意味的象征表现死亡：骑马的骷髅握着镰刀，前景的蛇象征诱惑与邪恶。他为这幅作品工作了数年，并一直不愿轻易将它交出。
lookForZh: 先辨认骑手的骷髅、手中的镰刀与前景的蛇，再沿赛道的弧线看一圈。把它当作画家对死亡和命运的表达，画面中的动物与人物便不只是赛马场的普通景物。

title: Twilight in the Wilderness
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
artistZh: 弗雷德里克·埃德温·丘奇
descriptionZh: 丘奇根据近两年前在美国缅因州卡塔丁山附近所作的写生，在纽约画室完成这片暮色荒野。作品诞生于美国内战前夕；馆方提出，炽烈的夕阳也可以被理解为对即将到来的战火的象征性暗示，这属于一种解读。丘奇曾让此画在知名画廊单独展出，并借助宣传吸引了大量观众。
lookForZh: 先比较天空中灼热的颜色与地面较暗的轮廓，再顺着水面和远山看向落日。可以分别体会它作为壮丽风景、以及作为时代情绪表达时带来的感受。

title: Church Street El
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 希勒从高处俯看纽约百老汇与华尔街一带，右侧可以看到教堂街的高架铁路。这一构图来自他与摄影师保罗·斯特兰德合作的短片《曼哈塔》中的影像。画家简化建筑形状，减少表面纹理，把注意力集中到几何形体、色块以及光影的节奏上。
lookForZh: 先找铁路与高楼之间的高度差，再把建筑暂时看作一组明暗不同的方块。沿这些形状的重复和错落移动视线，体会画家怎样把城市组织成有节奏的画面。

title: The Large Plane Trees (Road Menders at Saint-Rémy)
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
titleZh: 大悬铃木（圣雷米的修路工）
descriptionZh: 梵高住在法国南部圣雷米附近的疗养院期间，获准外出描绘自然。这幅秋景画的是工人在巨大的悬铃木下修整路面的场景；他给弟弟提奥的信也提到了沙堆、石头、发黄的树叶以及间或露出的房屋和小人物。馆方的保护研究认为，克利夫兰所藏的是这一构图的第一个版本。
lookForZh: 先看巨大树干怎样分隔街道，再找修路工人、沙石和树叶间露出的房屋。比较树木的尺度与人物的大小，体会这些普通街景怎样被安排得充满力量。

title: The Red Kerchief
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 画中人是莫奈的第一任妻子卡米耶。一个下雪的日子，她从阿让特伊家中的玻璃门外走过，画家捕捉了她投来的短暂一瞥。面部只由迅速落下的少量色点构成，积雪与树木也由较宽、断续的白色和绿色笔触表现。馆方说明，这幅画对莫奈很特别，他终身将其留在身边。
lookForZh: 先找雪景中醒目的红色衣物，再通过门框和玻璃看人物的脸。靠近时观察色点，退远一点再看表情怎样重新出现，体验画家如何留下转瞬即逝的一刻。

title: Cupid and Psyche
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 作品取材于丘比特与凡人普绪克的爱情故事：丘比特每晚来见她，但要求她不能知道自己的身份。大卫借此讨论理想爱情与身体现实之间的冲突。与常见的完美少年形象不同，他把丘比特画成带着得意表情、姿态略显笨拙的年轻人。馆方指出，这种处理也受到古代文献中顽皮而不友善的爱神形象启发。
lookForZh: 先比较丘比特的神情与熟睡的普绪克，再寻找画中的两只蝴蝶：一只在她上方，另一只在床架底部。人物的表情和小细节会改变整幅神话场面的气氛。

title: Portrait of a Man, Possibly Girolamo Rosati
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
titleZh: 男子肖像，可能为吉罗拉莫·罗萨蒂
descriptionZh: 这位衣着考究的男子身份与手势仍有讨论空间。他可能正要起身、向画外的人示意，或指向某处。桌上的植物与花朵带有爱情、纯洁和婚姻的象征意味，因此有人认为作品原来可能与新娘肖像成对。另一种解释将人物认作费尔莫官员吉罗拉莫·罗萨蒂，纸张也可能是建筑设计。馆方没有把这些解释定为唯一答案。
lookForZh: 先看伸出的手、桌面纸张和人物视线，再留意华贵衣料与花草。可以尝试两种阅读：他是在向亲近的人表达感情，还是在谈论一项事务；画面保留了这种悬念。

title: Elizabeth Shewell West and Her Son, Raphael
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
titleZh: 伊丽莎白·谢韦尔·韦斯特与儿子拉斐尔
descriptionZh: 韦斯特画的是自己的妻子伊丽莎白和儿子拉斐尔。他曾在意大利学习三年，十分推崇文艺复兴画家拉斐尔，甚至用这位大师的名字为长子命名。这幅温柔的母子双人肖像，在构图上借鉴了拉斐尔著名的《椅中圣母》。家庭成员由此进入了带有古典艺术意味的亲密场景。
lookForZh: 先看母亲与孩子彼此靠近的身体和姿势，体会两个人如何形成一个整体。再观察视线与手部动作，留意家庭肖像中温柔、安静的一面。

title: Portrait of Tieleman Roosterman
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 蒂勒曼·罗斯特曼是哈勒姆一位富有的亚麻布和丝绸商人，哈尔斯为他作画时，他36岁。人物姿态自信，黑色服装看似克制，却布满编带、纽扣和缎带饰花，宽阔的亚麻领子与带花边的袖口显示着财富和时尚。哈尔斯鲜明可见的笔触，让这幅正式肖像仍显得鲜活。
lookForZh: 先比较大块黑衣与明亮领口，再细看袖口、纽扣和腰部装饰。远看感受人物的气势，近看辨认大胆笔触如何共同组成昂贵面料的质感。

title: The Sacrifice of Isaac
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 作品描绘《创世记》中亚伯拉罕准备献祭以撒、却被天使及时制止的时刻。这幅画没有完成，因此也留下了安德烈亚·德尔·萨尔托的工作过程：他先把草图转移到木板上，再用薄层颜色逐步调整人物。天使、以撒身体与亚伯拉罕头部的改动仍可辨认，右侧驴子的线条也能帮助理解起稿的方法。
lookForZh: 先看父子的表情与身体动作，再寻找天使两组仍可见的腿部轮廓。未完成的地方让你直接看到画家如何修改，而不只是看到最后定稿的形象。

title: Hunting near Hartenfels Castle
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
titleZh: 哈尔滕费尔斯城堡附近的狩猎
descriptionZh: 这幅热闹的狩猎图由萨克森的新教统治者委托创作，远处建筑是他们居住的哈滕费尔斯城堡。左下角的约翰·弗里德里希穿着深绿色猎装，准备弩箭；右侧的妻子西比勒正准备作出仪式性的第一射。这类宫廷围猎需要猎犬、随从与号角信号配合。右下角的飞蛇是克拉纳赫的签名，数字1577则是收藏清点编号。
lookForZh: 先从近处贵族的动作看起，再沿河流寻找猎犬与鹿群。背景中还有熊和三头野猪；把这些细节逐一找出，会更容易理解整场围猎的复杂安排。

title: The Holy Family on the Steps
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 普桑以清楚的色彩、简洁形体和几何布局，组织了一场有关圣家与救赎的宗教思考。中央的玛利亚展示圣婴；左侧的圣伊丽莎白预示他的死亡，幼年施洗约翰递出的苹果关联《创世记》中人类的失落。右侧约瑟手中的圆规既提示木匠职业，也带有宗教象征。这些日常物件让看似简单的画面具有多层含义。
lookForZh: 先看人物如何排列在台阶上，再追踪各人的手势与目光。接着找苹果和圆规，比较人物之间的联系与红、黄、蓝等主要色块怎样让构图保持清楚。

title: The Crucifixion of Saint Andrew
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 作品描绘圣安德烈受难的基督教故事。按馆方介绍，他因拒绝承认异教神明而被钉上十字架，行刑者后来试图解开绳索，却被奇迹阻止。卡拉瓦乔让这场事件显得近在眼前，人物围绕受难者聚集，强烈明暗对比带出神圣意味。虽然圣安德烈通常与X形十字架相联系，这里使用的是竖直十字架。
lookForZh: 先看光照在哪些脸与身体上，再辨认周围人物的动作。留意深暗背景怎样压缩空间，让你仿佛站在事件旁边；也可以观察十字架形状与常见圣安德烈形象的差别。

title: The Burning of the Houses of Lords and Commons, 16 October 1834
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
artistZh: 约瑟夫·马洛德·威廉·透纳
descriptionZh: 1834年10月16日，伦敦议会大厦发生大火，民众聚集在泰晤士河边观看。最初的低潮妨碍取水和消防船只行动，火势持续数小时。特纳以这场真实灾难为出发点，夸大火焰的高度，用耀眼色彩和变化的烟雾、水气表现人面对巨大破坏力量时的无助；右下角的船只正驶向火场。
lookForZh: 先看炽亮火焰与河面的倒影，再找右下角的小船和岸边人群。比较微小的人与船、大片扩散的光和烟，体会画面的尺度差距。

title: Water Lilies (Agapanthus)
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 莫奈晚年长期描绘自己在吉维尼设计和培育的花园。这幅横向展开的睡莲池景，把目光集中在阳光穿过水面和被水面反射的一瞬间。画家省去了地平线与岸边，使池水看起来仿佛没有明确边界；巨大的横幅形式又进一步扩展了这种感受。
lookForZh: 先辨认哪些形状像浮在水面的植物，哪些像天空或树木的倒影。让目光横向缓慢移动，留意水面、倒影与水下空间怎样交织在一起。

title: The Power of Music
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 场景设在美国内战前的长岛乡村：一位非裔劳动者专注地聆听白人男子演奏小提琴。音乐让人物共享同一段体验，但他们分处谷仓门的内外。馆方认为，这扇门以及人物的空间分隔，同时表现了当时美国社会鲜明的种族界限。
lookForZh: 先辨认谁在演奏、谁在聆听，再看谷仓门如何把他们分在不同空间。试着同时感受音乐带来的联系和门所形成的隔阂。

title: Saint Peter Repentant
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 拉图尔把圣彼得画成一位反思往事、陷于悔恨的老人。作品关联彼得在耶稣被捕时否认认识他的故事；泛红的眼睛与摇曳不定的灯光暗示不安和难眠。低调的色彩、简单的形体让情绪更加沉静。旁边的公鸡则呼应耶稣关于彼得在鸡鸣前将三次否认他的预言。
lookForZh: 先从灯光照亮的脸和双手看起，再寻找公鸡。比较亮处与深暗背景的范围，体会少量光线怎样承载人物的疲惫与自省。

title: Wrestlers in a Circus
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
artistZh: 恩斯特·路德维希·基尔希纳
descriptionZh: 基希纳描绘两名摔跤手在鲜艳垫子上紧紧缠斗的场面。他以松动、迅速的笔触表现身体运动时难以看清的轮廓，把城市娱乐中的激烈瞬间变成有冲撞感的画面。馆方提示观众想象身处喧闹的比赛现场，从中体会作品的强烈感官效果。
lookForZh: 先追踪两名摔跤手交缠的四肢，再看身体与彩色垫子之间的对比。不要急于把每条轮廓辨认得很清楚，可以感受笔触本身传出的运动与不稳定。

title: La Cervara, the Roman Campagna
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
artistZh: 让—巴蒂斯特·卡米耶·柯罗
descriptionZh: 柯罗根据户外的素描与油画习作完成这幅大型风景。他在1825至1828年居住罗马期间，经常到周边乡村写生。作品通过一连串斜向延伸的地形组织远近层次，构图严谨，体现了他早年的风格，也让人联想到17世纪画家普桑的古典风景。
lookForZh: 先找近景中通向远处的斜线，再沿它们看向层层展开的田野。留意地形与明暗如何引导视线，即使没有复杂情节，也能让空间显得稳定而深远。

title: Danaë
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 作品取材于达娜厄的神话：她的父亲害怕自己被外孙杀死的预言，将她囚禁；朱庇特却化作从天而降的黄金前来与她相会。真蒂莱斯基借鉴了卡拉瓦乔面对模特作画、把人物推近画面的办法，同时通过柔和的笔法与优雅手势赋予场景诗意。
lookForZh: 先看从上方降落的金色细节，再观察人物姿态、手势和轻薄织物。比较肌肤与纱巾的不同质感，体会近距离人物带来的真实感。

title: Mount Sainte-Victoire
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 塞尚在生命最后二十年里反复描绘家乡附近的圣维克多山。这次，他把画架放在从艾克斯向东延伸的一条小路边，将近处的两棵伞松与远山纳入同一视野。一根树枝从左侧横过天空，呼应山体的斜坡，把近景与远景联系起来。
lookForZh: 先比较左侧横伸树枝的走向与远山斜坡，再看树木之间露出的景色。跟随这些呼应关系移动视线，体会近处植物如何与远山共同支撑画面。

title: Romaine Lacaux
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
artistZh: 皮埃尔—奥古斯特·雷诺阿
descriptionZh: 这可能是雷诺阿最早的署名油画。他在巴黎附近巴比松的艺术家聚居地停留时，接受度假的拉科一家委托，为孩子作了这幅肖像。白色上衣与背景帷幔的光亮色调来自他对半透明材料和反射光的观察，脸部细腻的色彩也体现了他早年瓷器彩绘训练的影响。
lookForZh: 先比较孩子面部、白上衣与背景的细微颜色，再看最明亮的地方。白色区域并不只有一种白，可以找出其中暖色与冷色的变化。

title: Christ and the Virgin in the House at Nazareth
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
titleZh: 拿撒勒家中的基督与圣母
descriptionZh: 苏巴朗描绘少年耶稣在编织荆棘冠时刺伤自己、玛利亚在旁流泪的场景。馆方认为，这个具体情节似乎是画家构想的，并非直接取自《圣经》；它用童年生活预示未来的受难。人物虽然高大庄重，画面却安静而亲密，圣母的泪水等细节尤其重要。
lookForZh: 先看少年手中的荆棘冠，再转向玛利亚的眼睛与泪水。留意桌面书本、水果和人物之间的距离，体会安静室内场景如何暗示未来的苦难。

title: Morning Glory with Black
sourceNote: 已于2026-10-04核对对应博物馆作品页；中文介绍为摘要，欣赏提示为编辑建议。；画名为直译，原文保留供核对
descriptionZh: 这幅1926年的布面油画将一朵牵牛花放大到几乎铺满画面。克利夫兰艺术博物馆说明，右下角露出的黑色花瓣属于另一朵矮牵牛。奥基夫让花瓣的曲线、明暗与色块本身成为观看的重点。
lookForZh: 欣赏提示：先沿着白色花瓣的边缘看一圈，再比较花心、白色花瓣和右下角黑色花瓣的明暗。试着把花当作几块弯曲的形状，看看画面如何保持平衡。

title: Green Tara
sourceNote: 已于2026-10-04核对对应博物馆作品页；中文介绍为摘要，欣赏提示为编辑建议。；采用常见题材译名；作者归属按官网保留不确定性
descriptionZh: 这是一幅约1260年代的西藏地区唐卡，即绘在布上的宗教图像。博物馆把作品归于尼泊尔艺术家阿尼哥，作者归属并非没有保留的确定结论。画面中央是绿度母；馆方说明，她右手下方的小僧人形象代表委托这幅画的人。2020年是装裱年份。
lookForZh: 欣赏提示：先看中央人物与周围小形象的大小关系，再寻找右手下方的委托者。观察绿色身体如何从周围装饰中凸显出来。

descriptionZh: 根据现有目录，《施洗者约翰的诞生与命名》由胡安·德·弗兰德斯创作，年代为1496—1499年，收藏于克利夫兰艺术博物馆。完整说明可查看本页所附的博物馆原始资料。

title: Portrait of Isabella Brant
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 伊莎贝拉·布兰特是鲁本斯的第一任妻子，他曾多次以不同方式描绘她。这幅肖像至少完成于她去世前五年。温暖的色调、丰润的笔触和生动神情，传达出画家与模特之间的亲近关系。馆方还指出，鲁本斯先画脸部，后来才补上双手。
lookForZh: 先看她的表情和温暖肤色，再观察脸与双手的处理。把注意力从身份服饰转向细微神情，更容易体会这幅肖像的家庭亲密感。

title: Portrait of the Jester Calabazas
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 卡拉巴萨斯是西班牙国王腓力四世宫廷中的弄臣，也是一位有身心障碍的人。委拉斯开兹以正式、全身宫廷肖像的形式表现他，并没有掩去身体特征。馆方强调，这种庄重的呈现方式赋予了当时常被视为边缘人物的人以强烈的人性尊严。
lookForZh: 先看人物如何完整地站立在画面中，再观察表情和手中物件：风车与小型女性肖像。可以比较正式肖像的规模与人物身份之间的关系，体会画家如何让他成为值得认真凝视的人。

title: Portrait of Catherine Grey, Lady Manners
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
titleZh: 凯瑟琳·格雷，曼纳斯夫人肖像
descriptionZh: 劳伦斯将爱尔兰诗人曼纳斯夫人表现为女神朱诺，孔雀是这一身份的象征。委托人却认为画得不够好看，拒绝接受作品。画家在1794年皇家美术学院展览中挂牌出售，但直到去世仍将它留在自己收藏中。作品流畅醒目的笔触和不同寻常的颜色，呈现了劳伦斯当时备受追捧的肖像风格。
lookForZh: 先寻找孔雀，再比较人物衣饰、背景与肤色的颜色。留意流动的笔触怎样营造华丽感，也可以思考这幅具有神话身份的肖像为何未必符合模特本人的期待。

title: The Dutton Family in the Drawing Room of Sherborne Park, Gloucestershire
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
titleZh: 格洛斯特郡舍伯恩庄园客厅中的达顿一家
descriptionZh: 这是一幅18世纪英国流行的家庭交谈画，以较轻松的场景表现一家人。父亲与女儿、母亲与儿子正围绕下一轮纸牌商量。家庭刚失去一位亲人，所以父母穿黑色重孝服，子女则穿淡紫、白与灰色的较轻丧服。馆方指出，室内陈设是理想化设计，反映他们希望拥有的时髦居所。
lookForZh: 先看两组家庭成员彼此靠近的姿态，再比较父母和子女衣服的颜色。纸牌场景显得亲密日常，服饰却留下了家庭正在哀悼的线索。

title: Panoramic View of the Alps, Les Dents du Midi
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
titleZh: 阿尔卑斯山全景：米迪群峰
descriptionZh: 库尔贝流亡瑞士期间描绘了从日内瓦湖向南望去的阿尔卑斯山景。作品原计划参加1879年的巴黎世界博览会，但他在1877年12月去世时仍未完成。部分区域用画刀厚厚堆叠颜料，右下角则保留未完成状态，让人能看见画家的不同工作阶段。
lookForZh: 先比较雪峰、云层的笔触与颜料厚度，再把目光移向未完成的右下角。不同区域的完成程度，让你看到一幅风景如何逐渐从画布上形成。

title: Mountain Market, Clear with Rising Mist
sourceNote: 已于2026-10-04核对对应博物馆作品页；中文介绍为摘要，欣赏提示为编辑建议。；画名据博物馆列出的东亚文字题名整理，原文保留供核对
descriptionZh: 这幅16世纪初的朝鲜王朝绢本水墨画，官网中文题名为《山市晴岚图》。馆方将画中的小人物解释为隐士及其友人：迎客、过桥和散步等场景散布在山水之间。作品曾被长期误认为中国北宋绘画，现按博物馆当前归类列入韩国绘画。
lookForZh: 欣赏提示：从左下方的院落开始，沿桥梁和山路寻找小人物，再看远处市镇。人物很小，却能帮助你理解山势的尺度和观看路线。

title: Books and Scholars’ Accoutrements
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 这类描绘书架、书籍与文房陈设的朝鲜绘画称为“册架图”，约从18世纪后半叶出现，19世纪广为流行，既进入宫廷，也装饰贵族书斋。画面右数第三扇藏着一枚印章，据此可以认出作者是19世纪后期的宫廷画家李宅均。
lookForZh: 先沿书架的格子寻找书籍和陈设，再到右数第三扇找隐藏的印章。比较各层架子的深浅与物件的摆放，体会画家怎样在平面上制造可进入的空间。

descriptionZh: 这幅1235年的高丽绘画描绘罗汉中的世供养尊者，原属一组五百罗汉像。馆方说明，尊者坐在竹凳上，正把龙引入钵中。作品以绢本水墨淡彩绘成。
lookForZh: 欣赏提示：留意人物侧面的姿态、手中的钵和面前的小龙，看看三个部分怎样形成一组相互呼应的动作。

sourceNote: 已于2026-10-04核对对应博物馆作品页；中文介绍为摘要，欣赏提示为编辑建议。；画名据博物馆列出的东亚文字题名整理，原文保留供核对
descriptionZh: 这组16世纪初的日本屏风以马厩为主题，由一对六曲屏组成。根据博物馆说明，马匹之外，画中还有驯鹰和围棋、将棋等活动；观看时可以把它当作由许多生活片段组成的长场景。
lookForZh: 欣赏提示：先找到马匹，再逐段寻找廊下的人物和他们的活动。比较马的动作与坐着下棋的人，体会画面的动静变化。

title: Operating on Guan Yu's Arm
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 葛饰应为以《三国演义》中关羽刮骨疗伤的情节为题：关羽中箭后接受治疗，身边侍从为所见情景惊惧，他却仍专注于对弈。画家用色彩强化戏剧性。她是葛饰北斋之女，在女性画家少见的时代与父亲合作，发展出自己的才能；馆方称这是她现存尺寸最大的画作。
lookForZh: 先比较关羽镇定的神情与周围侍从的反应，再看人物视线和色彩如何把注意力引向治疗与棋局。作品的戏剧性主要来自不同人物对同一时刻的反应差异。

title: Dragon and Tiger
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 虎坐在被烈风吹动的竹林中，龙则穿过云层，盘旋在翻腾波浪之上。龙虎在中国传统观念中关联阴阳与相互平衡的力量，也有虎啸生风、龙起生云的说法。馆方提出，这对屏风可能与依据《易经》的军事占候观念有关，表现世界不断变化的状态。
lookForZh: 先比较虎周围的风与竹、龙周围的云与水，再追踪线条的方向。两幅画既形成对照，也通过运动感相互呼应，可以把它们作为一对来欣赏。

title: Swift Bull from the Ten Swift Bulls
sourceNote: 已于2026-10-04核对对应博物馆作品页；中文介绍为摘要，欣赏提示为编辑建议。；画名据博物馆列出的东亚文字题名整理，原文保留供核对
descriptionZh: 这是日本《骏牛图》手卷中的一段，年代为13世纪末至14世纪初，后来改装为立轴。馆方说明，原卷画有十头牛，画家以不同比例的墨和水叠加，表现牛身体的立体感。
lookForZh: 欣赏提示：比较牛身上最深与最浅的墨色，观察身体轮廓与体积如何被区分出来。再看看四肢和头部的方向给你怎样的行动感。

title: Still Life with Meat, Fish, Vegetables, and Fruit
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 画家摆出种类丰富的肉、鱼、蔬菜和水果，器皿从陶器到昂贵的中国瓷器不等。对17世纪观众而言，这种丰盛可能让人联想到没有匮乏和饥饿的理想世界，也体现国际贸易带来的奢侈品。吃过的食物和翻倒的杯子暗示用餐者刚离席，昆虫正探索桌上的残余。
lookForZh: 先看器皿材质的差别，再找被吃过的食物、倒下的杯子与小昆虫。把它想成刚结束的一餐，会发现静物画里也有时间和人的活动留下的痕迹。

title: Snowscape with Figures
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 这是一幅罕见留存的朝鲜王朝早期绘画。馆方把雪山、树木和书斋中的独处学者，与画家退居隐逸的经历联系起来：画面既表现专心读书的隐居理想，也可能寄托他对家族政治失势后的感受。远处空着的木桥，又为幽静山居留出与外界相通的线索。
lookForZh: 先在大片雪景中找到书斋里的学者，再沿木桥观察内外空间如何连接。可以比较人的微小尺度与山林的广阔，体会画面中的安静和隔绝感。

title: Birds and Flowers
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 这对花鸟屏风把季节变化安排成从右向左的展开：从早春梅花一路延伸到较晚的秋季景物。中央的游鸭周围分布着鸢尾和桔梗；右侧猛禽惊扰雉鸟与白鹭，左侧则有孔雀相对。馆方将鹰与武力、孔雀与文化声望相联系，因此热闹的自然场景也带有身份象征。
lookForZh: 从右向左看一遍，寻找花木的季节变化，再比较猛禽与其他鸟类的关系。也可先找中央三只游鸭，用它们作为观察整对屏风的起点。

title: Mandala of the Three Shrines at Kumano
sourceNote: 已于2026-10-04核对对应博物馆作品页；中文介绍为摘要，欣赏提示为编辑建议。；画名据博物馆列出的东亚文字题名整理，原文保留供核对
descriptionZh: 这幅14世纪日本绘画从俯视角度表现熊野三山神社。馆方说明，画面把那智、新宫、本宫由上至下叠放，并在神社建筑上方用圆形区域呈现对应的佛教形象；右上方的瀑布为那智瀑布。
lookForZh: 欣赏提示：先分清上、中、下三组建筑，再找右上的瀑布和沿途人物。画面把不同地点放进同一空间，适合慢慢逐层观看。

title: Portrait of Ōzora Buzaemon
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 大空武左卫门身高超过七英尺，1827年到达江户后成为引人围观的人物，手印和木版画像都被当作纪念品。渡边华山在一位儒学学者家中见到他，并借助类似暗箱的投影工具，为绘画准备了这幅素描。馆方认为，画像表现出他被人盯看时的不自在。
lookForZh: 先观察人物的面部和姿态，不急于只关注他的身高。把线条中的拘谨与“被围观”这一背景联系起来，会更容易理解画像所保留的个人感受。

title: Winter Landscape
sourceNote: 已于2026-10-04核对对应博物馆作品页；中文介绍为摘要，欣赏提示为编辑建议。；画名据博物馆列出的东亚文字题名整理，原文保留供核对
descriptionZh: 这幅16世纪的朝鲜王朝山水画以水墨为主，局部略施淡彩。馆方说明，印章上的“Yeoseol”意为“如雪”；画中的岩石轮廓、树干线条和深浅墨色，共同把视线带向远处寒冷的山峰。
lookForZh: 欣赏提示：从画面下方向远山看，比较轮廓线和成片墨色各起什么作用。放大后可以留意马鞍与随从背负物上的浅蓝色。

title: Seven Jeweled Mountain
sourceNote: 已于2026-10-04核对对应博物馆作品页；中文介绍为摘要，欣赏提示为编辑建议。；画名据博物馆列出的东亚文字题名整理，原文保留供核对
descriptionZh: 这幅19世纪末的十扇屏风描绘朝鲜半岛七宝山。博物馆把它列为描写实际名胜地形的山水作品：画家采用俯瞰角度，将山峰、岩柱与陡峭崖壁铺陈在连续的屏面上。
lookForZh: 欣赏提示：先横向浏览整幅山势，再比较不同岩峰的轮廓。留意屏风的分段如何与山水的连续空间结合。

title: Hell Courtesan
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 河锅晓斋多次描绘传说中的“地狱太夫”。据传，她在遭遇劫持和苦难后，以带有佛教地狱图像的衣服表达对前世罪业的理解。这一版本作了诙谐改编：太夫对应七福神中的弁才天，其余神明出现在外衣上，其中一位向正在判案的阎魔王报告罪过。这里讲述的是传说与画家的改写。
lookForZh: 先看人物整体姿态，再把外衣当作另一幅小画仔细找神明与判案场景。衣上多次出现的金银色“寿”字，也能帮助你发现庄严、苦难与喜庆元素如何混在一起。

title: Medicine Master Buddha and the Twelve Divine Generals
sourceNote: 已于2026-10-04核对对应博物馆作品页；中文介绍为摘要，欣赏提示为编辑建议。；画名据博物馆列出的东亚文字题名整理，原文保留供核对
descriptionZh: 这幅13世纪的日本佛教绘画以药师如来为中心，两侧有日光、月光菩萨，周围环绕十二神将。馆方说明，药师如来左手持药壶，十二神将的发饰或头饰上有各自的生肖标志。
lookForZh: 欣赏提示：先找中央人物手中的药壶，再逐个观察外围神将的姿态和头饰。比较主尊的安定姿态与周围人物的动作。

title: Paulownias and Chrysanthemums
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 酒井抱一在这幅屏风中运用了“渗入”技法：在尚湿的颜色上滴入墨或色，让它自然汇聚，形成树皮斑点和叶片变化。桐与菊既关联季节，也与日本皇室纹章有关；馆方还指出，桐可带有坚毅的寓意，菊则可以象征良好治理。
lookForZh: 先近看树干上的斑点和菊叶的深浅变化，寻找颜色自然流动汇聚的痕迹。再退后看植物整体的轮廓，体会偶然水痕与精心安排的构图如何合作。

title: The Fourth King of Hell
sourceNote: 已于2026-10-04核对对应博物馆作品页；中文介绍为摘要，欣赏提示为编辑建议。；画名据博物馆列出的东亚文字题名整理，原文保留供核对
descriptionZh: 这幅14世纪末的高丽佛教画原属十王图组画，描绘第四王五官王。馆方说明，中央的王与侍从在上方审视判决的执行，下方呈现地狱惩罚场景；这些形象承担劝诫的宗教作用。
lookForZh: 欣赏提示：留意上方审判者与下方受罚场景之间的分区，以及人物大小和位置怎样表明各自的角色。画面含有惩罚场景。

title: Orchids and Rocks
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 作者李昰应既是19世纪朝鲜的重要政治人物，也是以兰花著称的文人画家。这幅八扇屏风只用水墨表现从峭壁垂下的兰叶，用弯曲的长线条组织画面。兰花生于野外而有幽香，常被文人用来寄托坚守操守的品格，因此它也具有超出植物外形的含义。
lookForZh: 先顺着兰叶从崖边向下的曲线移动目光，再比较浓墨、淡墨与空白的分布。注意同一种植物怎样通过线条的疏密、长短和方向，在八扇屏风间形成变化。

title: Grapevine
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 这幅八扇屏风描绘夏日风雨中的葡萄藤，藤蔓跨过画面，几乎形成一个大圆。画家用不同浓淡的墨色表现暴风雨中的快速运动。馆方介绍，葡萄很早便成为东亚的艺术题材，到19世纪后期，大串果实也常被用来象征子孙繁盛。
lookForZh: 先沿藤蔓的大弧线看完整幅屏风，再比较果实、叶子和枝条的墨色。留意哪些线条像被风拉动，感受静止的水墨画怎样表现夏日风暴。

title: Standing Ksitigarbha
sourceNote: 已于2026-10-04核对对应博物馆作品页；中文介绍为摘要，欣赏提示为编辑建议。；画名据博物馆列出的东亚文字题名整理，原文保留供核对
descriptionZh: 这幅1300—1350年间的高丽绘画，将地藏菩萨表现为年轻僧人。馆方说明，他手持锡杖和宝珠；这些物件与地藏救度受苦众生的宗教含义有关。作品以墨、颜色和金绘在绢上。
lookForZh: 欣赏提示：从面部、双手一直看到足下，留意锡杖、宝珠与衣纹。比较细密的装饰与整体垂直姿态如何共同营造宁静感。

title: Nathaniel Hurd
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 纳撒尼尔·赫德是波士顿著名的银匠和雕刻师。科普利笔下温暖的目光与自然微笑，暗示了两位艺术家之间的友谊。敞开的衣领和略微斜戴的头巾代替了当时正式肖像常见的假发，使人物显出少见的轻松与随意。
lookForZh: 先看眼神和嘴角，再比较敞开的领口与头巾。把这些细节与常见的严肃礼服肖像相比较，就能体会这幅画像熟人相见般的亲近。

title: Cloudy Mountains
sourceNote: 已于2026-10-04核对对应博物馆作品页；中文介绍为摘要，欣赏提示为编辑建议。；画名据博物馆列出的东亚文字题名整理，原文保留供核对
descriptionZh: 米友仁于1130年绘制的《云山图》是一卷绢本水墨设色山水。克利夫兰艺术博物馆说明，他南渡后到达浙江新昌，以此画感谢提供庇护的主人。米友仁和父亲米芾以湿润墨点层层积成山形，营造烟云笼罩的氛围。
lookForZh: 欣赏提示：先把画卷横向浏览一遍，再靠近看山头的墨点。观察深浅墨色与空白怎样让山峰仿佛从雾中浮现，而非依靠清楚的外轮廓。

title: Portrait of a Family Playing Music
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
titleZh: 演奏音乐的一家人肖像
descriptionZh: 这家人的身份仍不清楚，但大理石地面与壁炉、桌上的祈祷毯和丝绸衣服，都说明他们生活富裕。右侧雕花柜上的中国瓷器和日本漆盒，联系着荷兰与亚洲的贸易。家庭中共同奏乐既是日常活动，在画里也可以象征家人关系和睦。
lookForZh: 先看人物怎样围绕音乐活动相互联系，再寻找瓷器、漆盒、织物与大理石。物件的材质和来源，可以帮助你从一个室内场景看到家庭财富与当时的跨国贸易。

title: Nur Jahan holding a portrait of Emperor Jahangir
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
titleZh: 手持贾汉吉尔皇帝肖像的努尔·贾汉
descriptionZh: 画中女子被认作莫卧儿皇帝贾汉吉尔的妻子努尔·贾汉，她手持丈夫的正式肖像。丈夫已显出年老的面貌，她自己却保持理想化的年轻形象。馆方认为，这种构图可能借鉴皇帝手持亡父画像、表明继承地位的做法；她曾处理大量政务，也希望在丈夫去世后继续掌权。
lookForZh: 先比较女子与手中画像里的皇帝的年龄表现，再看“画中画”如何建立两人的关系。可以把这幅作品同时看作人物肖像与对政治身份的表达。

title: Seventy-Two Peaks Under the Blue Sky with Mount Furong
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
titleZh: 青天七十二峰与芙蓉峰
descriptionZh: 题记把景色指向中国湖南衡山的七十二峰，特别提到其中的芙蓉峰。屏风较低，馆方推测它可能用于小茶室中的隔断。松村吴春可能受到老师与谢芜村的启发，后者晚年也画过同一山系。金银箔上的绘画，让简洁山景兼有表面光泽与深远空间。
lookForZh: 先看山峰之间的留白，再留意金银底色在山水之间露出的地方。可以想象这件低屏风放在茶室时，观看者较近、较低的视线会怎样改变看山的感受。

title: Portrait of a Government Official
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 这位官员穿深绿色朝服，坐在覆盖豹皮的椅子上；豹皮是朝廷赠给新任官员的礼物。胸前绣有单鹤的补子表明他的官阶为三品。蔡龙臣细致表现了人物略显羞涩的微笑，馆方将它解读为新任官员面对未来仕途时，自信与不安交织的心情。
lookForZh: 先看胸前单鹤与椅上的豹皮，辨认身份线索，再把注意力转到嘴角和眼睛。正式服装与细微表情放在一起，让官员的社会地位和个人情绪同时出现。

title: Mme L . . . (Laure Borreau)
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 这是库尔贝为洛尔·博罗夫人所画四幅肖像中最后、也最充分完成的一幅。她穿黑色蕾丝装饰的丝裙，戴相配帽子，背景有金色与紫色的夕阳。库尔贝坚持描绘可见的现实，保留眼部阴影和颈部的真实形态，没有把人物一味美化，当时甚至因此遭到批评。
lookForZh: 先比较黑色衣裙的细节与背景柔和的金紫色，再看面部和颈部的明暗。可以体会画家怎样在华美的肖像形式中，保留一个具体人物的身体特征。

title: View of Schroon Mountain, Essex County, New York, After a Storm
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
titleZh: 暴风雨后纽约州埃塞克斯县施伦山景色
descriptionZh: 科尔在初夏观察这处阿迪朗达克山景，回到画室后却把它改成灿烂的秋色，以表达对美国荒野的赞美。画家将山峰称作“施伦山”，实际名称是霍夫曼山。右前景的树叶间还画有两名原住民；馆方指出，当地原住民当时正承受白人移民、采伐、采矿和旅游业不断扩张带来的压力。
lookForZh: 先看暴风雨后的光与秋叶颜色，再到右前景寻找两个人物。景色的宏大与人物的微小可以同时观看，也能提醒我们这片风景中有人居住和生活。

titleZh: 阿玛贝尔与玛丽·杰迈玛·约克小姐肖像
descriptionZh: 阿梅贝尔与玛丽·杰迈玛姐妹正在伦敦郊外家族庄园的庭院中玩耍。她们穿的是为这幅肖像特别构想的宽松衣服，服饰与环境共同凸显家族地位。雷诺兹从意大利归来后把古典艺术经验带进构图：右侧女孩护住鸽子、不让家犬靠近的姿态，呼应古罗马的持鸽少女雕像。
lookForZh: 先辨认姐妹各自的动作，再看鸽子与狗怎样带出一小段互动。留意宽松衣料和优雅姿势，体会普通游戏场景如何被画成带有古典意味的家族肖像。

titleZh: 王子与苦行者，选自沙贾汗晚期画册
descriptionZh: 画面表现莫卧儿王子拜访一位住在洞窟附近的苏菲圣人。它原本是较早的独立作品，后来被装入沙贾汗画册的新边框。圣人面前的海螺用来宣告祈祷开始，前景一对鸭子被馆方解释为精神生活与世俗生活和谐相合的象征。页边还分布着多位苦行者形象。
lookForZh: 先看王子与圣人的相对位置，再找地面的海螺和前景双鸭。最后观察边框人物，体会中央相会场景与四周宗教形象怎样共同构成这一页。

title: Calligraphy and Painting Party
sourceNote: 依据克利夫兰馆方作品数据整理；欣赏提示为编辑建议。
descriptionZh: 这是一幅多人合作完成的画：河锅晓斋先画聚会人物，以及屏风、画卷的外形，再由十位文人补入其中的书画，每件小作品都带有署名。中根半岭用饱蘸墨的大笔写下“寿”，福岛柳圃画屏风梅花，松冈环翠画莲花。场景表现艺术家响应客人请求、当场挥毫创作的聚会。
lookForZh: 先把画中不同屏风和书画卷一一找出，再看人物似乎在指向或展示哪些作品。还可以寻找正在打盹的人，体会正式创作与热闹、随性的聚会气氛如何共存。

descriptionZh: 高更在法国西北部蓬塔旺画下这位扑向海中的女性。馆方把这一形象解读为现代欧洲女性放弃文明约束、投向自然的隐喻。简化的轮廓与夸张的绿、橙对比，带有强烈的主观安排。1889年作品在巴黎伏尔皮尼咖啡馆展出，体现了高更以形象和颜色表达象征意义的方向。

descriptionOriginal:
Sixteen children engage in scholarly, religious, and military activities, representing the popular “one hundred boys” theme expressing the wish for abundant, successful male offspring. Such paintings conveying auspicious wishes were often displayed during the New Year festival season.

Two older boys wear small crowns with red tassels. Another child with a mask holds a brush in one hand, a rice measure in the other. He stands on a low table imitating Kuixing, the God of Examinations and servant to the God of Literature.

title: Ramblers over a Winding Stream
descriptionZh: 右侧过桥的小人物是一群闲游的士人。前景树干盘结、枝条弯曲，馆方把这种“蟹爪”树法与北宋画家郭熙的传统联系起来。

descriptionOriginal:
This album leaf is one of few surviving paintings by Luo Zichuan. During the Yuan dynasty, the Luo family of painters in Jiangxi province, in Southern China, had a network of patrons extending their reputation all the way to the capital city of Beijing.

The small, rounded figures crossing the bridge on the right are gentlemen enjoying a ramble, rather than ascetics or travelers. The composition is dominated in the center foreground by “crab-claw” trees with knotty trunks and twisting branches. Their robust forms show Luo’s connection to the earlier master, Guo Xi (about 1020–about 1090).

creatorsOriginal.biography: Luo Zhichuan was part of a local school of painting based in Xinyu 新喻, Linjiang 臨江 circuit, Jiangxi province in the late Southern Song and early Yuan periods.

verificationLevel: 官方 API 图文同编号核对

descriptionOriginal:
This set of four seasonal landscape hanging scrolls are by Ren Yu. He was the youngest, most eccentric, and least prolific of the Four Rens, a family of prominent painters in Shanghai during the late Qing dynasty (1644–1911). Perhaps due to his opium habit and subsequent financial difficulties, Ren Yu tended to be lackadaisical in his work. The few remaining high-quality paintings hint at his artistic potential lost to opium.

Though Ren’s premature death left his artistic promise unfulfilled, his paintings were acquired and donated to the museum by Charles Lang Freer (1854–1919), a wealthy businessman and art collector from Detroit. As Freer had hoped, this donation of Ren Yu paintings inspired the young Cleveland Museum of Art to continue to expand its own Chinese painting collection.

creatorsOriginal.biography: Ren Yu 任預 (1853–1901) was the youngest, most eccentric, and least prolific of the Four Rens (Ren Xiong, Ren Xun, and Ren Yi [Bonian]) a family of prominent painters in Shanghai during the late Qing dynasty (1644–1911).

techniqueOriginal: Set of four hanging scrolls; color on paper

descriptionOriginal: A miniature inspired by the “Peach Blossom Spring,” this painting illustrates the well-known tale written by the poet-recluse Tao Yuanming (365–427 CE), in which a fisherman accidentally discovers a hidden utopian village where residents live in harmony, untouched by the outside world's troubles. descriptionOriginal:
This minimalist landscape places most of the representational elements in the lower right foreground. A lone gentleman strolls along a zigzagging path by the water. With the gentleman’s staff acting as a visual cue, the viewer’s gaze is directed to geese flying over distant mountains.

The scene of a marshland, with its wet and soft ground dotted with vegetation, suggests springtime in Jiangnan. Combined with the flying geese, the album evokes the poetic lines:
By spring fields, geese are about to return,
Under chilly waters, fish are submerging.
春郊欲回雁, 寒水正沉鱼

descriptionOriginal:
Throughout his lifetime, Xiao Yuncong visited Nanjing and Yangzhou, cities embedded in the fertile and water-rich Jiangnan region, as reflected in his paintings. Xiao painted from nature, and his landscapes are informed by the seasons and his travels, as well as by his experience as a print designer. Xiao’s fresh, light colors continue to appear in later Shanghai school paintings.

This album was formerly in the collection of Li Yufen in Yangzhou and then owned by Wu Hufan in Shanghai. While the artist impressed his seal consistently below his poetic inscriptions in the upper parts of the composition, the red seals on the margins and in the lower corners of the paintings are impressions by the album’s previous owners.

descriptionOriginal: Zha Shibiao, a native of Anhui province, moved to Yangzhou later in his career, like so many of his fellow countrymen. At age 68, he painted this album with seasonal landscapes in various styles. Painted in fresh colors and wet strokes, all depict typical scenes of Jiangnan, the Yangzi delta: a herdboy on a buffalo wading through water, boating on the stream to the Peach Blossom Spring at Wulin, a waterfront town shrouded in mist, a scholar on his donkey enjoying the red autumn leaves, and drinking tea on a boat while watching migrating birds.

descriptionZh: 牧童坐在树下，身边有水牛、牛犊和八哥。馆方指出，牛既是田园生活的主角，也曾被用来比喻勤勉、承受劳作的人。

descriptionOriginal:
Here, a herdboy tending a cow with a calf is sitting beneath a tree with his pet myna bird. The painting can be read as a pastoral scene. As the water buffalo helped plow the fields, it was perceived as an animal that endures hard work without gain for itself, often interpreted as a metaphor for the official.

Ox-herding pictures, presented as gifts in court circles, were used for their moral and political rhetoric. The Yijing (Book of Changes) states, The Receptive is the earth, the mother . . . it is a cow with a calf . . . the multitude [in relation to the ruler].
didYouKnowOriginal: Li You included such tiny details as circular patterns of hair on the buffalo’s hindquarters.

descriptionOriginal: This leaf presents a rising promontory in the near distance, whose base is hidden by a dense grove of barren, autumnal trees. A gentle incline emerges from the lower right, with a small path leading to its summit, where a gentleman is sheltered from the wind by two pines. This promontory resembles Guangming Ding 光明頂 (Summit of the Bright and Luminous), the second tallest peak in Huangshan 黃山 (Mt. Huang or Yellow Mountain), the scenic area that inspired much of Mei Qing’s artistic production. Instead of looking down on the “Sea of Clouds,” though, as one who scales Huangshan’s peak would, this gentleman is looking out at two boats on an actual sea.

descriptionOriginal: The court artist Li Song from Hangzhou excelled in meticulous depictions of children, peddlers, and their various goods. Painted during the reign of emperor Ningzong, the drama unfolding around vulnerable children may allude to Ningzong’s nine sons who died young, leaving him without a direct male descendant.

descriptionOriginal:
Wu Bing, a native of Piling, gained Empress Li’s favor and served as a painter-in-attendance at the court in Hangzhou during the Shaoxi reign (1190–94). The round fan painting shows a dragonfly hovering over a stalk of bamboo, a bush cricket (luowei) perching on a leaf, and a flying wasp.

Yellow leaf tips suggest the late summer or early autumn season. The chirping of the cricket sounds similar to the sound of a working loom; the insect is therefore also called weaving lady (fangzhi niang). The weaving season starts when the weather is about to turn cold—the cricket symbolizes early autumn.

descriptionZh: 长卷依次描绘乾隆、皇后和十一位妃嫔，各像绘于不同阶段。馆方说明，最初三幅由郎世宁绘制，其余由中国宫廷画家续绘。

descriptionOriginal:
This portrait shows the Qianlong emperor at 26, in the first year of his reign. His likeness is followed by portraits of the empress and eleven consorts. Their portraits document the appearances of the court women around the time when they received their respective imperial titles, which occurred at different stages of the emperor's life. The first three portraits were done by the Jesuit (Roman Catholic) missionary artist Giuseppe Castiglione, whereas the later ones were by Chinese court painters.

Formal portraiture contributed to the affirmation of status and construction of role and identity. This scroll served as both familial documentation and a "mind picture" of the Qianlong emperor, suggesting that his constructed image of emperorship was inseparable from concepts of self and family. It was stored in a carved red lacquer box bearing the original painting title Mind Picture of a Well-Governed and Tranquil Reign (see CMA 1969.32).

title: A Vignette of Life on the Frontier
artist: Jiao Bingzhen (Chinese, active c. 1670–1726) [artist]; and Giuseppe Castiglione (Italian, 1688–1766) [artist]
descriptionZh: 这把扇面的场景和驯马人由焦秉真绘制，马由郎世宁加入。两位画家保留各自的表现方法，同时让人物、柳树与马协调相处。

descriptionOriginal:
Jiao Bingzhen, a court painter largely active during the reign of the Kangxi Emperor, was the senior artist on this fan. Jiao painted the Manchu horse trainer and the setting into which the horse was inserted by Giuseppe Castiglione. Each artist was bonded to his own artistic tradition, while flexibly and harmoniously accommodating the others’ style.

Jiao’s brushwork displays rigor and control, particularly in the twisting and turning trunk of the willow. The treatment of the figure and his clothes is an exercise in linearity. The horse trainer’s gesture and posture closely adhere to the known repertoire of the Chinese figural tradition, but the specificity supplies a sense of documentary reportage of life on the frontier. His shaved forehead and white temples identify him as a Manchu. The thick fabric of his garments was defined in a different sort of brush line than Jiao typically used for Chinese scholars or travelers.

Jesuit priest Castiglione, a newcomer to China at the time this was painted, brought a sense of Western realism to the horse. Poised at a slight angle, the horse is alert, its eye gleaming. Its contours suggest the bulk of its anatomy with skilled but not overpowering modelling, and careful and subtly wrought attention to detail, such as fluttering strand of mane.

Because of his ability to combine traditional Chinese painting techniques with Western methods of perspective and chiaroscuro, Castiglione went on to be the most favored and honored of the missionary artists who served the early Qing emperors. Throughout his career, in addition to imperial demands for portraits and records of court events, Castiglione continued to paint favored imperial horses. These animal subjects reflect the desire of Kangxi and his successors to celebrate their nomadic origins and to keep alive the martial prowess of the Manchu warriors in their new and sedentary world of conquered China.

descriptionOriginal:
The twenty paintings in this double album by Chen Hongshou include landscapes, figures, and flowers. It also has one leaf featuring a woman, an often-used subject not found in the other albums from the latter part of his career. His late works are wonderful summations of Chen's peculiar and quirky art—archaistic, hyper-refined—but without accompanying shallowness or sentimentality.

His figures and landscapes in the late albums are miniaturized, not unlike the small Chinese gardens, or the carefully selected small table rocks or old roots used for contemplation to see the world in miniature. This loss of scale is quite deliberate and reflects the psychological situation of a depressed class like the Ming loyalist officials and scholars, deprived of their integrity and honor, and forced to lead a diminished and restricted existence.

By the 1360s, when the Red Turbans began to rebel against the Yuan dynasty leaders, and the Mongols gradually lost control over Jiangnan, Wang Meng withdrew into the mountains north of Hangzhou, calling himself Woodcutter of Yellow Crane Mountain. In the early years of the Ming dynasty, Wang was caught up in a purge and died in prison.

descriptionOriginal:
By the 1500s, visits to historic and scenic sites in the lower Yangzi delta stimulated an increase of printed illustrated travel books. Topographical depictions of local scenery flourished.

Leaves from this album illustrates sites around Lake Tai of the two adjacent counties Changxing and Wuxing (modern Huzhou). Song Xu, who lived intermittently in Jiaxing and Songjiang, must have passed through Wuxing by boat and thus knew the region.

The paintings are inscribed with gazetteerlike notations, suggesting that the album was produced for clients as commemorative works, a travel guide, or for “armchair travel” (woyou) in one’s mind.
didYouKnowOriginal: Song Xu favored a painting style that was technically polished and focused attention on specific, realistic details.

creatorsOriginal.biography: Song Xu (宋旭, 1525–c. 1606), was a versatile Chinese painter active in northern Zhejiang and Jiangsu provinces. He was skilled in landscapes, boundary paintings (界畫, paintings of architecture), figure painting, and Buddhist painting. Although born a commoner, he also cultivated the literati arts of poetry and calligraphy. He studied Chan Buddhism and eventually became a Buddhist priest himself.

descriptionOriginal:
Herdboys tend their buffalo in a bucolic landscape by a winding stream. Guo Min emphasizes the massive forms and mighty power of the animals, transforming them into forces of nature.

The poem in the first scroll reads: "The bulls are engaging in fighting, Cautiously, each seeks to overcome the other. The herdboy calmly stands by. Untying his belt, he silently watches."

The poem in the second scroll reads: "Together, they wade through the middle of the stream, Mindless of perils in the journey. The grass grows tall in the village ahead, While the mist and rain spread far and wide."

descriptionOriginal:
This painting captures a squirrel in action, distracted and twisting its head while climbing and looking at a little bug to the right. The painter skillfully employs a combination of ink washes and fine brushstrokes to simulate the animal’s fur. Only three simple curved lines depict the squirrel’s claws.

The subject of squirrels did not appear in Chinese painting before the late Southern Song (1127–1279) and Yuan periods (1279–1368). The painter Songtian was one of the few Yuan painters who specialized in this theme.

descriptionOriginal:
Few works by the Yuan workshops in Yangzhou present a continuous composition of such monumental scale as this hanging scroll. Road to Shu (in Sichuan province) depicts the trade of goods over long distances and through mountainous terrain. Busy travelers lead mules over footbridges, mountain paths wind along steep slopes, and soaring bridges connect peaks divided by deep gorges.

The Yuan studios produced paintings to decorate the residences of wealthy Yangzhou salt merchants and princely palaces. The title Road to Shu refers to the historical drama of the flight of Tang emperor Xuanzong (reigned 712–56) to Sichuan in the aftermath of the An Lushan Rebellion (755–63). At the same time, the scenery alludes to Anhui, the mountainous native country of many of the salt merchants and their trade routes in northern parts of the empire.

descriptionOriginal:
Bamboo is an evergreen plant that does not break under the weight of snow or the force of the wind, and thus became a favorite motif in literati painting and Chan Buddhism as a metaphor for the virtue of not yielding to worldly temptations.

Xuechuang, also known as monk Puming, was a native of Songjiang, near Shanghai, who spent his life as a monk in Suzhou. In 1338, he presided over Yunyan temple on Tiger Hill. Here, he masterfully depicts a bamboo gently bent in a subtle breeze. Puming’s paintings were revered in Japan and Korea.

descriptionOriginal:
Wang Hui studied paintings by earlier masters and digested their styles with unceasing virtuosity. He had such enduring affection for a landscape by Wang Meng 王蒙 (about 1308–85) that between 1686 and 1712, he made several copies, like this example. One of his compositional transformations here was moving the scholar from the pavilion directly into the landscape by the stream.

His faithful copying also included inscriptions. Wang Meng had written that he was trying to resuscitate the style of an earlier artist, Wen Tong (1018–1079); therefore, Wang Hui sought to revive both Wang Meng and Wen Tong.
didYouKnowOriginal: As a leading figure in the Orthodox School of Chinese painting, Wang Hui believed that the act of painting was a dialogue with one or more masters of the past.

Two figures sit conversing in a thatched cottage. This painting illustrates two poetic lines:

My guest came to sit beyond the dust,
In a narrow room, we talked about the autumnal sounds of autumn.

The cool wilderness depicted in this work conveys an aloofness that may reveal the inner world of a scholar-artist who failed the civil service examination but preserved a sense of pride and endurance in his humble surroundings.

descriptionOriginal:
Lin Bu (967–1028), a Northern Song (960–1127) poet and hermit who lived at the West Lake in Hangzhou, was known for having plum trees for his female companions and cranes for his children. This hanging scroll depicts the poet walking in the moonlight and looking at the plum tree, a scene described in his most well-known poem on plum blossoms.

Surviving works signed by Du Jin are rare and this painting is one of them. Here, the artist used lively brushwork to depict the plum tree and rocks, exemplified in varying dots and strokes, and sweeps in different shades of ink.

descriptionOriginal:
Wang Yuanqi, an official in Emperor Kangxi’s (reigned 1662–1722) court, grew up in an artistic family. Like other mainstream painters of the Orthodox School, he followed a canon of earlier styles and artists endorsed by Ming calligrapher Dong Qichang (1555–1636).

Here, Wang drew inspiration from Ni Zan (1301–1374), a Yuan dynasty painter known for his simple compositions and spare use of ink. Master Ni seldom used color, but Wang added green and ochre washes to the trees, cottages, and hills in this landscape. Painting was a way for Wang to relieve the pressures of his official duties.

descriptionOriginal:
Similar to some calligraphers of his time, Zhu Da rejected conventions in favor of an individual, personal expression. He is known for ambiguous compositions of fish, flowers, birds, and rocks in contrasting ink tonality. As a member of the Ming imperial family, Zhu lost his princely status and hid in a monastery when the Manchus, foreigners from the north, established the Qing dynasty in 1644.

In this late work, mountain ranges are rendered in diverse and dense strokes rising toward the top of the scroll. It references the artist Dong Qichang (1555–1636) in concept. Yet the cursory brushwork and composition present Zhu’s personal style.
didYouKnowOriginal: Zhu Da's inscription acknowledges that this painting was done after the early Song master Guo Zhongshu 郭忠恕, but there is almost no tangible stylistic relation to be found between Zhu Da and his 10th-century model.

descriptionOriginal:
The dragon and tiger are tied to the philosophical concept of yin and yang, which describes opposite but complementary forces. The dragon occupies a tiered background of waves and mist. Its luminous head emerges from the darker passages, and its narrow twisting body is serpent-like. By contrast, the close-up view of the tiger emphasizes its bulk. The tiger bends its head to lick its paw while its tail curls in the foreground.

In their original Chan Buddhist context, this pair of scrolls likely flanked a central image, like the Bodhisattva Guanyin. The silk has darkened over the centuries, and the slight reddish shading in the tiger’s tongue and nose has faded.

descriptionOriginal: This masterfully composed landscape in light colors and delicate brushwork is an image of the water-rich Jiangnan region in southeast China, where Wu Bin was active as an artist. Lantern displays and street performances in the villages salute the New Year, and are interwoven with scenes of farming, fishing, and silk making. descriptionOriginal:
Yun Shouping came from Piling (modern Changzhou), Jiangsu province, a center of floral, plant, and insect painting. He had joined the anti-Manchu resistance, was briefly imprisoned, and witnessed the death of family members in 1644.

Like other artists, Yun Shouping expressed his Ming loyalism in coded pictures. The peony, king of flowers, and a spring garden motif developed new meaning during the Qing dynasty. The inscription indicates that Yun turns the flower into a motif representing the glorious past. The herbaceous peonies here appear somewhat withered and pale, with faint reddish veins running through its broken branches, perhaps a coded message.

The inscription reads,
An old painting by an anonymous painter of the Northern Song Dynasty has five varieties of flowers painted in the boneless manner. Its colors are so beguiling and beautiful, that even after several hundred years its lead pigments are like new. The skill with which the ink and colors were applied and the subtlety of its composition find no equal among modern followers.
didYouKnowOriginal: In East Asian art, peonies traditionally symbolize prosperity and wealth.
techniqueOriginal: Hanging scroll; ink and color on silk

They had encountered before, during which Daoxin advised the Pine Planter to endure a reincarnation as he was too old to reach enlightenment. title: Ink Flowers
artist: Zhao Zhong (Chinese, second half of the 1300s) [artist]
descriptionZh: 赵仲为花卉配诗，用细线与层层淡墨表现本可设色的花叶。馆方认为，不同季节植物的组合也可能与画家的医学背景有关。

descriptionOriginal:
Zhao Zhong's flowers, each paired with a poem, echo the fine-style colored flowers of the academic tradition, but instead he used only ink. Fine lines define the contours of each plant, as well as the veins within each petal and leaf. Careful ink washes give subtle modeling to the forms.

The combination of lily, narcissus, and peony is unusual as the three belong to no known seasonal or symbolic system popular in the fourteenth century. Zhao’s medical training may have influenced the selection. Powdered lilies, for example, were prescribed to dispel grief, while the bark of tree peony roots was used as a treatment for various blood disorders.

descriptionZh: 蓝瑛以支遁、许逊清谈的古代故事赠给僧人友人，用历史人物映照彼此的友情。作品创作于明朝灭亡前一年。

Lan Ying’s painting is a gift to his friend, the Chan monk Wuyun, in which he depicted two sages of the Six Dynasties period: the Buddhist monk Zhidun (314–366 CE), and the Daoist priest Xu Xun (265–420 CE). Meant to be understood as an analogy of the friendship between artist and monk, the painting also offered a retreat into the past, a year before the fall of the Ming dynasty.

A professional painter born in Hangzhou, Lan Ying is traditionally considered a last representative of the Zhe school. Lan wrote poetic inscriptions and interacted with the literatus Chen Jiru (1558–1639).

descriptionOriginal:
In this scene, windswept rain pelting a village captures the power of nature in a masterful composition.

Lü Wenying from Zhejiang served as a court painter during the Hongzhi era (1488–1505). Hardly known, with few remaining works, he is considered a Zhe school painter who followed the style of the Southern Song academy. Zhe school painters, named after the province of Zhejiang, transformed the poetic scenery of the Southern Song artists into dramatic, large-scale views. Active in the same region with frequent monsoon rains in the summer season, artists were familiar with outbreaks of rain and storms.

Seasonal paintings, including those depicting flowering plum trees in early spring, furnished scholars’ studios or other interior spaces in the house.

Peng Xu is considered the foremost follower of the famous plum blossom painter Wang Mian (1287–1359) (see CMA 1974.26). The branches are brushed in the same vigorous manner leaving white streaks in the ink indicating the gnarled bark. The delicate blossoms are drawn in fine lines, while a gray wash covers the entire surface, only leaving the flower petals in reserve.

title: Lily and Butterflies
descriptionZh: 萱草与蝶鸟相伴，羽尾、叶片和花瓣的线条彼此呼应。馆方说明，萱草在传统语境里常与母爱相联系。

descriptionOriginal: The bird is represented in pale ink, probably sketched in before the darker ink was used to finish the rock. Like the butterfly and moth above, his tail feathers echo the bamboo as well as the leaves and petals of the flowers. The Chinese wagtail can connote brotherly love. The daylily was used for various pharmaceutical purposes, especially for deadening pain in childbirth. It was also considered efficacious in relieving grief and aiding in the production of sons. The lily is in fact the real subject of this painting: it is the common symbol for motherly love. Hence, the lingering of the butterfly over a lily can signify a son's love, devotion, and yearning for his mother—the refuge from worldly woes.

title: Portrait of An Qi
artist: Wang Hui (Chinese, 1632–1717) [artist]; Tu Luo (Chinese, active c. 1715) [artist]; Yang Jin (Chinese, 1644–1728) [artist]
descriptionZh: 盐商、收藏家安岐被画成自然中的隐者，身边的书、琴、太湖石和仙鹤带出文人生活的理想。作品由三位画家合作完成。

descriptionOriginal:
An Qi, the subject of the portrait, was a second-generation salt merchant from Korea. He used part of his wealth to collect art. At the time this painting was commissioned, An was less than 40 years old. He is represented as a Daoist recluse in nature, informally dressed with attributes such as books and a wrapped guqin instrument, a portrait convention for literati-scholars since the Six Dynasties period (220–589 CE). The local Taihu rock, banana plants, and crane suggest a southern garden and a life in seclusion. An’s portrait is evidence of merchants aspiring to the scholar-official class.

According to the inscription, this painting was the joint effort of three men, the eldest and most famous was Wang Hui. While the garden setting is homogenous in style, it contrasts with the application of opaque pigments and shading employed for the depiction of An Qi’s face.

leading Nanjing school artist Gong Xian (on display nearby). When the Ming dynasty collapsed in 1644, Tao joined the loyalist resistance in Yunnan province. By 1645 the Manchu invaders had defeated the Yunnanese forces, prompting Tao to flee to Burma, where he died shortly thereafter. Only five of Tao Hong’s works are known to exist, of which this painting is the largest.

title: White-Robed Guanyin
descriptionZh: 白衣观音坐于岩石之上，净瓶、竹枝与光环共同构成慈悲的宗教形象。馆方将作品归于张月壶名下，并保留“传”的限定。

descriptionOriginal:
The figure here sits on a rocky elevation representing Potalaka in the Southern Sea, Avalokitesvara’s island home. A vase with a bamboo sprig holds pure water, the nectar of life. Bamboo shines through the figure’s halo, a way of seeing the illusionary world through the Buddhist truth.

Avalokitesvara (Guanyin in Chinese), the bodhisattva of compassion, was integrated into the Chan Buddhist canon of venerated beings. In this context, the bodhisattva is often depicted in its female manifestation as the White-Robed Guanyin. The worship of the feminine White-Robed Guanyin has its origins on Mount Tianzhu in Hangzhou, where Qian Liu (852–932), ruler of the Wuyue kingdom, established the Upper Tianzhu Monastery to venerate her image.

Wang Mian from Zhejiang province had failed the civil and military service examinations and later rejected appointments under the Mongol government. Instead, he chose to return home, making a living by selling plum paintings. Few of Wang’s works have survived, but they demonstrate that by his time the ink-plum (momei) genre was fully developed.

title: Portrait of Priest Dazhi (1048–1116), Master of Law
artistZh: 画家佚名、劉 燾（题字）
descriptionZh: 元照法师手持钵与锡杖，被表现为行脚僧。刘焘是题赞者；馆方据身后追赠的称号判断，这幅像作于法师去世以后。
lookForZh: 先看人物的姿态和视线，再比较衣纹、饰物与背景。可以想一想，这些细节如何让人物显得亲近、庄重或疏离。

descriptionOriginal:
Monk Yuanzhao, with the honorific title Dazhi Lüshi, Great Wisdom Master of Vinaya, is depicted here as an itinerant monk, holding his alms bowl in the left and staff in the right. In 1142, Emperor Gaozong had bestowed Yuanzhao with a posthumous title, mentioned in the inscription, which suggests that the portrait was made after the master’s death. A master of the Lü sect of Buddhism, with a calm benevolent smile on his face, Yuanzhao was active on Mount Tiantai and in Hangzhou. Later, Liu Tao, a southerner from Changxing, added the inscription.

The eulogy reads:
Dignified he is, perfect in his upasampada [ordination of a monk]. His appearance is like his mind. Uncompromising and aloof. His mind is like his appearance. To say he is square, he proves to be round. He looks timid, yet his spirit is unbound. Having no attachment, and holding no reins, men and deities alike take refuge in him. —translated by Wai-Kam Ho
didYouKnowOriginal: A native of Hangzhou, the priest Dazhi was known for his eloquent exposition of Buddhist doctrines and for his success in winning many converts.

title: The Hermit Xu You Resting by a Stream
descriptionZh: 许由拒绝帝尧让位后隐居耕作，画中他穿着简朴、闲坐溪边。左侧山体与右侧空白形成对照，人物的从容神态成为重点。

descriptionOriginal:
Xu You, a recluse who refused the throne offered to him by legendary Emperor Yao, chose instead to farm on Mount Ji. Sitting under cliffs, his left arm resting on his risen leg and his loose robe revealing his belly, he displays a nonchalant attitude. Xu You is wearing a laborer’s outfit, a short robe and tight leggings, while his composed pose and gentle features reveal his lofty character.

The composition shows rising mountains on the left juxtaposed by open space on the far right. Powerful brushstrokes and nuanced ink washes follow the style of the Southern Song (1127–1279) academy painters.
didYouKnowOriginal: When the emperor offered him a post overseeing the Nine Territories (as China was known in ancient times), Xu You went to the River Ying to cleanse his ears from such an unwelcome proposition.

title: Dream Journey to Mt. Tiantai
descriptionZh: 钱杜把天台山的石梁、瀑布和密集崖壁组合成梦中游历的景象。亭内人物回望溪谷，给宏大的山水加入了人的观看位置。
lookForZh: 先辨认画面中的人物和主要动作，再看视线怎样在各部分之间移动。这里的提示是观看方法，可结合原图自行观察。
sourceNote: 图像与资料来自克利夫兰艺术博物馆官方 API 同一作品编号；中文简介据馆方说明摘译，赏画提示为观察建议。
descriptionOriginal:
When he painted Mt. Tiantai 天台山, Qian Du was a mature artist with a distinctive style that balanced refinement and “studied awkwardness.” He included the site’s famed features: the crescent-shaped stone bridge arching across the waterfall and surrounded by dense cliffs. Rows of pine and other vegetation appear in the crevices above and below the mountain. The twisting trunks and branches are left in outline, encased within the variegated foliage. In a pavilion at the center, a man and a woman look back to the lower right, across the ravine and toward the cascading water. Beyond and to the left, two simple mounds are backed by hills that stretch into the distance.

Qian Du left space above the hills for an inscription describing the circumstances that gave rise to the painting. Chen Wenshu, family friend and patron to Qian Du, had dreamt of a journey to Tiantai, a mountain famed for both its natural beauty and its associations with legends and myths. This short handscroll was based on Chen’s description of his dream journey, on which he marveled at the scenery and encountered a goddess. Six months after the painting’s completion, Qian transcribed his friend’s longer poetic reminiscence on paper mounted after the painting.

The landscape of the painting was not based on the physical site, which likely neither man had visited in 1814, but rather on the mythic tradition of Tiantai. It caused turbulence in the mind of the poet and provided inspiration to the painter.
didYouKnowOriginal: The man and woman in the pavilion likely represent Chen Wenshu and the mysterious presence he encountered on his dream journey to Mt. Tiantai.

descriptionOriginal: Li Shan was born into a family of scholars and officials in Yangzhou. The wealth and status of Li's family assured him an educational and cultural advantage, including his appointment at court. The subjects Li Shan chose to paint—orchids, bamboo, pines, and flowers—reflected his literati background. Five Pine Trees, painted late in his career, is an unconventional work. Rather than having focused on a realistic treatment of the subject, Li created the trees with an interplay of richly modulated strokes, while he utilized a semicursive script among the branches to illustrate the kinship between painting and calligraphy.

title: Zhongli Quan Crossing the Ocean
descriptionZh: 钟离权是八仙之一，画中他正渡海而行。飘动衣纹和翻卷波浪带来强烈动感；作品没有署名，馆方依风格将它归于赵麒。

descriptionOriginal:
Here, Zhongli Quan is crossing the ocean. He is one of the Eight Immortals (baxian), a group of popular Daoist figures who understood the way of life and could transform into otherworldly beings. Zhongli Quan is usually depicted as a scholar with a big belly seen through his partially open robe. The artist used expressive brushwork to depict the immortal’s fluttering robe and the roaring waves, skillfully creating a sense of movement.

This scroll may have been one of a set depicting the Eight Immortals. Although the painting has no signature or seal, its style supports an attribution to the Ming dynasty painter Zhao Qi.

Many of his paintings lament the loss of the empire. In this scroll, he depicts a lone figure in a stark landscape of frosty atmosphere enshrouded in mists. Close looking reveals red strokes that color the grounds, a way of expressing his loyalty to the Ming whose family name Zhu means red.

With a fine ink line and graded wash, the life-like depiction of these swiftly moving carp is representative of the high quality of works by Liu Jie, a Ming dynasty court painter known for his fish paintings. The artist’s signature and seal are in the painting’s top left corner.

The carp is an auspicious and popular subject in Chinese painting. Here, the leaping carp can be associated with “a carp jumping the dragon gate,” which according to mythology transforms into a dragon, emblematic of a scholar’s success in passing the civil service examinations. Another reading suggests that this carp is not leaping but guiding his offspring in worshipping heaven.

descriptionOriginal:
Guanyin, the bodhisattva of infinite compassion (Avalokiteshvara, in Sanskrit), reveals himself in many forms. According to Buddhist belief, one such manifestation is the white-robed Guanyin sitting on a rock on the island of Putuo (Potalaka, in Sanskrit), located along the coast not far from Ningbo, in Zhejiang Province, China.

Here, the figure was swiftly drawn in only a few ink lines. The inscription above is by Zhongfeng Mingben, perhaps the most widely respected and influential Chan (Zen in Japanese) master in the Yuan dynasty. The artist’s signature is a single line below on the left: Huanzhu Yongzhong.

One squirrel perches on a branch nibbling a chestnut, while the other on ground is approaching a fallen chestnut. The painter used fine, short staccato strokes to simulate the animal’s soft fur, while the tree is depicted with broader wet strokes in a rougher manner.

Ge Shuying is known for his depictions of squirrels in a monochrome style characterized by crisp, decisive brushstrokes. From there his works spread to Japan, where squirrel paintings gained the attention of Japanese collectors.

In this typical southern two shores divided by a river composition, two fishermen, each seated in the stern of his covered houseboat, troll their hooks in the swirling water, holding short rods fitted with spooling reels.

Zhao Yong was a son of the southern calligrapher and statesman Zhao Mengfu, who, like his father was a scholar-official in the Mongol-Yuan government. The landscape in deep green tones offers a view into a secluded mountain valley, populated by ancient figures surrounded by deer and cranes, all under high pine trees. A red-robed immortal in the air steers his crane toward the paradise land.

This idyllic scene was presumably created amid the tumultuous transition from the Yuan to the Ming dynasty. Chen from Suzhou supported major rebel leaders, first Zhang Shicheng (1321–1367) with his base in Suzhou and then his rival Zhu Yuanzhang in Nanjing, after the latter had established the Ming dynasty. Chen was executed in 1371.

title: Streams and Mountains
descriptionZh: 无数披麻皴把层叠山石连成统一节奏，山脚的林荫间藏着隐居之所。画中访客步行而来，让高耸山景有了亲切的生活线索。

descriptionOriginal:
Like many literati of the late Yuan and early Ming dynasties, Xu Ben was entangled with the perils of dynastic change as well as the ups and downs of his official career. It was mainly through the art of painting and poetry, as well as the ideal of reclusion, that he sought feelings of exhilaration and shared them with his friends.

Xu created this monumental landscape during one of his periods of reclusion. His innumerable “hemp-fiber” texture strokes create a unifying rhythm among the towering mountains with tightly knit masses of rocks. Nestled among shady trees at the base of the mountain is a rustic retreat, which a scholar approaches on foot to visit with the hermit.

Among the five inscriptions at the top of the painting is one by the artist himself. He dedicated the painting to someone named Jifu 吉夫 and recorded a poem in praise of mountains.
Green trees, yellow orioles, everywhere are mountains;
Aimlessly I return from the stream, where I watched the clouds.
Man's life does not allow unbroken ease,
But to be able to be high up in the mountain, this is leisure.
didYouKnowOriginal: An attendant opens a reed gate to welcome the scholar with a walking stick approaching the rustic retreat.

The artist may have intentionally extended the branches beyond the paper to emphasize the abundance of fruit. Xugu’s subjects of flowers, goldfish, and loquats express wishes for abundance and wealth, and must have appealed to his patrons.

Xugu gave up his career as a military official during the Taiping rebellion (1850–64) and became an itinerant monk who painted for a living. He spent the later years of his life in Shanghai and his fame as an artist is associated with that city.

title: Cleansing Medicinal Herbs in the Stream on a Spring Day

descriptionOriginal: A famous portraitist, Yu Zhiding here depicts the likeness of Shi Shenyi 史申義 (1661–1712), an official and poet. Master Shi, a sickly man, was deeply interested in medicinal science. The opening section of the scroll features a boy washing a fungus in fresh spring water, a basket of medicinal herbs by his side. Other servants carry a fan, a bundle of scrolls, and a cup of tea or hot wine. Master Shi sits in a bamboo grove, surrounded by fields of herbs. Returning swallows, pink peach blossoms, and blooming magnolia indicate spring, whereas the fungus conveys wishes for long life. The spring theme may express the artist’s wish for his friend’s recovery.

This portrait was jointly executed by Wei Shijie and Hua Yan himself who painted the landscape in the background. Hua Yan is shown here at the age of about 23. The sword at his back is a reference to his early desire for a military career, while the scholar’s robe suggests an opposing aspiration. Together these are signs of a complex personality.

descriptionOriginal:
The large red tripod-shaped seal on this painting is that of Kano Motonobu, head of the Kano school atelier in Kyoto that served the shogun. Gesshū Jukei, a longtime resident of the Zen temple Kenninji in Kyoto, inscribed the poem. The two are known to have worked together on at least one other occasion. The poem describes an intimate meeting of dear friends, a suitable theme for a work that was likely given as a gift to an esteemed associate, perhaps weary of the politics of life in the capital.

In either fine weather or
during the rainy season the
mountain’s color is pale.

A friend visits, rowing his
boat while reciting a poem.

Tonight we’ll drink
together at the inn on the river.

Across, on the other side of the
river is a house with people
living in it, but there
is nothing to drink there.

Fills my heart with grief.

descriptionOriginal: Fujiwara no Kintō (996–1075), a Japanese courtier, scholar, and poet, compiled select examples by the most celebrated composers of 31-syllable poems (waka) from the 600s to the 1000s. Painters soon made these “thirty-six poetic immortals” a favorite subject, traditionally presenting the poets in sequential, idealized portraits paired with their poems. In this interpretation, a chronologically impossible gathering of these great talents is in progress. The screen’s composition follows one devised by design virtuoso Ogata Kōrin (1658–1716).

descriptionOriginal: Kyoto-based painter Sōami adapted the small-format Chinese album leaf and handscroll painting compositions belonging to the Ashikaga shogunate to the large-scale paintings he created for residences and Buddhist temples. As curator of the shogunal collection, Sōami would have carefully examined its Southern Song and Yuan dynasty Chinese paintings, gaining specialized knowledge of a variety of brush modes, including the soft style used for this painting. The scene is part of a continuous landscape once mounted in the folding screen format. Removed from the screen, this section of the painting was cut down, given new backing papers and a textile mounting with a hanging cord at the top and a roller with knobs at the bottom so that it could continue to be appreciated.

descriptionOriginal: This is one of two paintings possibly by Sesshū Tōyō. They once flanked a central scroll with an ink landscape. The unbalanced nature of the compositions, however, suggests they may be images recycled from larger paintings. The one with sweet osmanthus and hibiscus is an autumn scene, the other is a summer scene with daylilies and gardenias. Folding screens often contrast two seasons or depict all four across a single pair of screens. Sesshū’s works were sufficiently prized that repurposing them in fragmentary form to display in an alcove of a luxurious room would not be an unusual choice.

descriptionOriginal: Kitagawa Sōsetsu painted for the Maeda family, powerful rulers of what is present-day Ishikawa Prefecture on the central northern coast of Honshū, Japan’s main island. Screens served as room dividers and backdrops in Maeda grand residences. This composition is considered one of the artist’s masterpieces. Kitagawa Sōsetsu is thought to have been a student of Tawaraya Sōsetsu, who was in turn the student of Tawaraya Sōtatsu the Kyoto-based master painter regarded as the creator of the style that came to be known as Rinpa. By selecting a painter of this lineage, the Maeda family consciously connected their aesthetics to those of the imperial capital as a means of proclaiming their elevated status.

descriptionOriginal: These four paintings originally decorated sliding doors that partitioned the interiors of Japanese buildings. Painters from the Kano school, named after the artist Kano Motonobu (1476–1559), were major forces in the production of screens and architectural interiors in Kyoto. When he headed the workshop, his work was prized by the upper strata of society. Kano is credited with combining the subtlety of Chinese black ink painting, as seen in the rocks and hills, with the color and realism of Japanese painting, seen in the birds and flowers. Landscape scenes like this were prized by the elite of Kyoto, both for their contemplative aesthetic and their patrons’ refined taste.

descriptionOriginal: This pair of screens shows a group of elite Chinese gentlemen and their servants in the countryside. One man is considering his painting in progress, while another looks on as two of his companions play a board game called qi, known in Japan as Go. Nearby is a table set with a selection of books ready to be read and a qin, a type of stringed instrument, still wrapped in its cloth case waiting to be played. descriptionOriginal: Ukiyo-e artists and collaborating poets introduced imagery from classical literature to add layers of meaning to their work. Here, a courtesan pores over a letter from an admirer, and the poem next to her reads as follows: "Having been asked to stay over, / I stayed on—and for a good reason. / It’s way past midnight / and the lady is that (legendary implorer) Amagoi Komachi." Midnight was closing time in Yoshiwara, the licensed brothel district of Edo (now Tokyo). Amagoi, or “Praying for Rain,” Komachi refers to ninth-century poet Ono no Komachi—known for her compelling verse and great beauty—and one of her famous compositions.

descriptionOriginal: Reeds and geese has been a common pairing in Chinese literary and visual culture for many centuries. This painting presents the contribution of a Japanese amateur painter, almost certainly a Zen Buddhist monk, to Japan’s fledgling efforts to add the theme to its own cultural vocabulary in the early 1300s. As was customary at the time in Japan, the painter did not sign or seal his work; the inscription, a poem added to the painting by the eminent émigré monk Yishan Yining, along with his signature and seal, was of far greater cultural value. Today, the modestly sized painting has tremendous significance as one of the earliest surviving examples of Japanese ink paintings with reeds and geese.
didYouKnowOriginal: Tokyo National Museum owns a copy of this painting made by Kano Gyokusen (1796–1864) when he was 14 years old.

The tall, flat-topped hat is an element of the native dress of the Mughals from eastern Uzbekistan. Of mixed Turkic and Mongol ethnicities, they spoke a Turkic language known as Chaghatai. Chaghatai refers to the name of the son of the Mongol Chingiz (Genghis) Khan, who ruled this area of Central Asia from 1246 to 1282.

This woman’s hat has been studded with jewels and strings of pearls. The portrait jewel format that was once reserved for the emperor has now been expanded to include ladies of the court. The woman holds a jade wine cup and wears a draped upper garment with a woven or embroidered border similar to the fragment on display at the left.

descriptionOriginal:
Drawings such as this served as models for formal painted portraits of Mughal and Rajput royalty in court workshops.

The confident contour lines, delicate shading, and subtle facial expression are the work of the master artist Nur Muhammad (active 1570s–1630s), identified in a Persian inscription on the back. He came from a distinguished family of artists who settled in Bikaner by the mid-1500s. Nur Muhammad also worked at the Mughal court, notably for the mother of Emperor Akbar (reigned 1565–1605). His descendants continue to be recognized as the master artists of Bikaner up to the present day.

descriptionZh: 作品描绘乌代浦尔君主贾加特·辛格二世的王室狩猎。山丘、植物、猎物与随行者组成细密场景，背面题记记录参与者身份。

descriptionOriginal:
One of the favorite pastimes of the Rajput nobility was hunting, a subject frequently depicted in secular painting in Rajasthan. Often much larger than other Indian paintings, hunting scenes glorified the pleasures and splendors of these stately affairs. This colorful painting depicts a royal hunt conducted by the Maharana Jagat Singh II of Udaipur. An inscription on the reverse side of the painting mentions the Maharana's name along with the hunting party's other participants, including the Maharana's brother.

The hunt takes place in a detailed landscape of hills and varied vegetation. The animals (tiger, bear, wild boar, deer, stag, and antelope) are rounded up and diverted by servants (who shoot firecrackers) toward the shooting box at the center of the composition, where the royal members of the hunting party await their prey. Another group of servants with dogs approaches from the opposite direction to cut off the animals' route of escape. Some beasts are already killed or wounded, while others are trying desperately to run for their lives.
didYouKnowOriginal: The painting is signed on the reverse by the artist—a rare occurrence in Indian painting. The name reads "Jugarsi, son of Jiva."

descriptionOriginal:
The Mughal emperor responsible for a revival of courtly arts and pastimes was Muhammad Shah (reigned 1719–48). This painting was made by an artist from a small kingdom in the western Himalayas who stayed at the Mughal court in Delhi and painted scenes of his experiences.

Like his predecessors, Muhammad Shah enjoyed watching elephant fights. He is shown in his window of public audience, marked by a golden carpet, smoking a hookah. Women from his harem can be seen looking on from behind painted screens.

Two pairs of men hold fire brands and spears to prevent the elephants from running off and to keep them under control. The intensity of the fight—captured at a moment when one mahout, or elephant trainer, has dropped his goad and is about to jump off—is augmented by the dense colors and forms in contrast to the otherwise pale planes, balanced only by the strip of palace windows.
techniqueOriginal: Gum tempera and ink on paper

descriptionOriginal: Clad in a straw rain poncho and wide-brimmed hat, a fisherman is seated in a small boat. Reeds sparkle on the far shoreline among dark, black rock forms that appear to float above the water. This landscape painting, which emphasizes an intimate solitary moment through evoking various atmospheric elements—rain, evening light, and frosty air—was one of the main subjects of mid- and late 16th-century landscape paintings.

descriptionOriginal:
In this hanging scroll, an egret walks along the shores of a salt marsh where reeds abundantly grow. Native to Pyongyang, the artist Yang Ki-hun had no rival in bird-and-flower themes. The Taedong River estuary, one of Pyongyang’s beloved natural sites, may have been Yang’s favorite spot to observe and sketch various water birds.

Yang treated his subjects of flora and fauna with an observant naturalist’s view, yet his choice of subjects—an egret and reeds—is deeply rooted in traditional symbolic language: the egret stands for the scholarly reclusive life, while reeds indicate humility and modesty.
didYouKnowOriginal: Yang Ki-hun was one of the most commercially successful painters known for decorative bird-and-flower subjects.

title: Peasants Smoking in an Inn
descriptionZh: 特尼尔斯以描绘17世纪佛兰德乡村生活见长。画中年轻人倚墙仰头，馆方将这种姿态解释为吸烟过度；旁边准备烟斗的男子带着逗趣的神情看着他。
lookForZh: 欣赏提示：比较三个人的头部、手部与身体姿态，观察这场小小的日常戏剧如何展开。
sourceNote: 图像与资料来自克利夫兰艺术博物馆官方 API 同一作品编号；中文简介据馆方说明摘译，赏画提示为观察建议。
descriptionOriginal: David Teniers the Younger was a popular artist who specialized in small paintings of rustic Flemish life in the 1600s. In works such as Peasants Smoking in an Inn, an older man and a younger man in the foreground smoke tobacco. The younger man rests limply against the wall and his head lolls back, a gesture that symbolized that he had overindulged in smoke. Another standing man prepares his pipe and watches the younger man with amusement. Tobacco was a novelty in the 1600s, introduced from the Americas and East Indies with other new imports such as sugar cane and rice, and was believed to be a medicinal product. It was particularly recommended for people who lived in "waterish places" such as Antwerp, the capital of Flanders, where Teniers painted this scene. Although many medical practitioners believed tobacco to be a cure for numerous ailments, moral opponents to smoking criticized it as a danger to health and morals. The mixed reputation and widespread popularity of tobacco smoking thus made it a marketable and amusing subject for Flemish artists such as Teniers.

descriptionOriginal: The seemingly weightless figures, the startling color combinations, and the moody, imprecise setting all show El Greco’s interest in conveying the intense spirituality of these figures rather than their concrete reality. Above all, the painting addresses Mary’s role as mediator between Christ and the viewer. She supports her son, but her faraway look indicates awareness of his fate. Mary feeds Jesus fruit held by Joseph that is full of symbolic meaning, with the apple representing the fall of man; cherries, the blood of Christ; peaches, salvation; and pears, the sweetness of Christ’s virtue.

descriptionOriginal: Like his colleague Claude Lorrain, Poussin depicted historical and mythological subjects in landscapes inspired by the countryside around Rome. His themes were often complex, and frequently incorporated witty allusions to classical texts. Here, a playful cupid tugs Pan, the goatlegged Greek god of the woods, toward Venus, the goddess of love. The painting cleverly illustrates the Latin phrase amor vincit omnia, or “love conquers all” (in Greek, pan means “all”). The woodland setting represents the idyllic paradise of Pan’s home.
didYouKnowOriginal: After arriving in Rome and experiencing financial instability, Nicolas Poussin turned to painting more popular, lucrative mythological scenes, such as those depicting nymphs and satyrs.

descriptionOriginal: The only assistant his famous uncle ever had, Gainsborough Dupont apprenticed with Thomas Gainsborough before setting up his own studio. It is often difficult to distinguish the late works of both artists. This painting is among Dupont’s best portraits. He captures the beauty of his sitter with soft, flickering brushstrokes, detailing her frilly collar and impressive hairstyle, curled and powdered according to the current style. This portrait originally hung alongside that of her husband Thomas in the drawing room of the couple’s home, Ammerdown House in Somerset, where Thomas’s portrait still hangs today.

descriptionOriginal: This painting is an example of a tronie, a Dutch word meaning “head” or “facial expression.” Tronies were not intended to be identifiable portraits, but artistic investigations of facial appearance and fanciful costume. Particularly in the years around 1630, Rembrandt used this popular format to explore different lighting effects and facial expressions. Here, the strong contrast of light and shade shapes the contours of the young man’s face; unusual accessories such as the striped scarf and glittering pendant on a jeweled chain add an exotic touch. Although this painting bears Rembrandt’s monogram, the authorship is not certain. Some scholars have attributed it to Isaac de Joudreville (1613–1648), a pupil and associate of Rembrandt who painted comparable tronies in a similarly smooth and elegant style.
didYouKnowOriginal: Once identified as Rembrandt himself, the sitter is now considered an anonymous study of human character.

descriptionOriginal: Although French by birth, Claude Lorrain spent his entire working career in Rome. He revolutionized the art of landscape painting by filling his harmoniously ordered scenes (inspired by the campagna, the countryside around Rome) with a golden, hazy light. Painted early in Lorrain's career, Italian Landscape shows a wide, sweeping vista with a wooded hill topped by a structure resembling an ancient Roman temple. The left side of the picture is dark, but the foreground sweeps away in a curve to the right that leads off into an increasingly luminous distance.

descriptionOriginal: Known as a tête d'expression or "expressive head," this painting represents an essential part of the academic training of history painters who specialized in religious, mythological, or historical subjects. In 1760, such exercises became standard at the École des Beaux-Arts (School of Fine Arts) in Paris, then known as Académie royale de peinture et de sculpture. Focusing on the relationship between morality and beauty, the goal of a history painter is not only to create a pleasing image, but also to represent the emotions of the soul.
didYouKnowOriginal: The high quality of this painting was of such renown that David’s students requested permission to copy it.

creatorsOriginal.biography: The founder and leading painter of the neoclassical movement in France, Jacques-Louis David was born in Paris to a prosperous family of artists and archi-tects. In 1766 he entered the Académie Royale as the pupil of Joseph-Marie Vien (1716-1809). After several failed attempts, David won the Prix de Rome in 1774. The following year he left for Italy, where he studied antique art and envisioned replacing the frivolity of the rococo with an art of grandeur, simplicity, and moral virtue. After returning to Paris in 1780, he established his reputa-tion with three spectacular successes at the Salon: The Oath of the Horatii (1785, Musée du Louvre, Paris), The Death of Socrates (1787, Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York), and The Lictors Bring-ing Brutus the Bodies of His Sons (1789, Musée du Louvre, Paris). Widely interpreted as moral parables for contemporary political events, these archetypes of neoclassical aesthetics set the standard for academic painting of the next century. In the 1790s David joined the radical Jacobin Club and played an active role in the French Revolution. He allied himself with Robespierre, served a short term as president of the Convention, and voted for the execution of Louis XVI. He also placed his artistic talents at the service of the Revolution by creating paintings that glorified its martyrs and by organizing public festivals that celebrated the new political order. As the most prominent artist in the revolutionary ranks, he led the attack against the Académie Royale that culminated in its abolish-ment in 1793. When the excesses of the Reign of Terror precipitated the fall of Robespierre in 1794, David was imprison-ed but spared execution. Authorities released him the following year due to ill health. Around 1798 David developed a new alliance with the brilliant young general of the Directory, Napoléon Bonaparte. David's painting The Intervention of the Sabine Women (1799, Musée du Louvre, Paris) coalesced perfectly with Napoleonic propaganda urging national reconciliation. After the coup d'état of 1799, Napoléon was named first consul and began supplying David with important commissions. Upon Napoléon's coronation in 1804, David was appointed first painter to the emperor. David's monumental painting The Coronation of Napoléon, or Le Sacre (1805-7, Musée du Louvre, Paris), introduced a less spartan, more colorful and emotive style. However, as seen in his life-size portrait Napoléon in His Study (1812, National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C.), David increasingly searched to balance this new heroic-romanticism with an exacting realism. In 1816, following Napoléon's defeat at Waterloo and the restoration of the monarchy, David went into exile in Belgium. He spent the last nine years of his life in Brussels, painting mostly mythological subjects and portraits. David died of a stroke in 1825 and was denied burial in France.

title: Diana and Her Nymphs Departing for the Hunt
artistZh: 彼得·保罗·鲁本斯及其工作坊
descriptionZh: 狄安娜额头上的新月同时表明她是月亮女神。鲁本斯把人物推向画面前方，使向前迈步的女神仿佛接近观者；左侧仙女抵挡萨堤尔的动作，也为出猎场面加入了寓意。

descriptionOriginal: Diana, the Roman goddess of the hunt, wears a crescent on her forehead, also identifying her as the moon goddess. Diana lived apart from men, accompanied by a group of nymphs; she often represented unattainable beauty or chastity. With a nymph at left fending off a lustful satyr, Rubens refers to a struggle between vice and virtue, combining a sensual display of female bodies with a moral undertone. To bring the viewer more fully into the narrative, Rubens pulls the full-bodied figures to the front of the picture plane, and Diana steps forward, activating the space between viewer and subject. The nymph at the right has the features of Isabella Brant, the artist’s wife, and can be compared with Rubens’s portrait of her, also in the museum's collection.
didYouKnowOriginal: The moon and stars on the white and black dog’s collar indicate that both hounds are companions of Diana, accompanying the goddess on her hunts.

titleZh: 装扮成圣塞巴斯蒂安的青年肖像
descriptionZh: 箭指向圣塞巴斯蒂安的身份，但人物的服装属于15世纪末，说明它是一位当时青年借圣徒形象呈现的肖像。作者曾在达·芬奇工作室工作，画中柔雾般的阴影也受到达·芬奇影响。

descriptionOriginal: Sebastian, a bodyguard for the ancient Roman emperor Diocletian, was shot with arrows and was eventually drowned for his commitment to Christianity. While the arrow alludes to Saint Sebastian, the young man’s clothing dates to the late 1400s, indicating that this is a contemporary portrait, rather than an image of the historical saint. This haunting image was influenced by the paintings of Leonardo da Vinci (1452–1519), particularly in the artist’s use of smoky shadows (called sfumato) to model the flesh. It was painted by Marco d’Oggiono, a Milanese artist who worked in Leonardo’s studio.
didYouKnowOriginal: While Marco d'Oggiono made numerous copies of the masterpieces of his teacher Leonardo da Vinci, this is an original composition.

descriptionOriginal: John Opie's working-class roots made him sympathetic to the plight of the laborer.
